meta: Scam messages used to be full of spelling mistakes, so you could spot them right away. Now scammers use AI too: in seconds they have a hundred smooth messages using your real name and where you work.

muc.title: Messages that look too right
muc.text: Scam messages used to be full of spelling mistakes, so you could spot them right away. Now they read just like a real bank.

muc.title: Scammers use AI too
muc.text: Because scammers use AI too. In a few seconds they have a hundred smooth messages, even using your real name and where you work.

muc.title: Stop checking the spelling
muc.text: So stop looking for spelling mistakes. Look at what the message asks you to do.

muc.title: Three dangerous requests
muc.text: Three red flags: asking you to click a link to log in, asking for a one-time code (OTP), or asking you to install a strange app. Real banks don't do that by text.

muc.title: Use AI against AI
muc.text: A good trick: paste the message into AI, hide your personal details, and ask: does this message show signs of a scam? AI points out red flags very quickly. But the final call is still yours: call the official hotline to ask.

muc.title: Don't click links
muc.text: To check your account, open the bank app you already have installed. Never click links in a text message.

muc.title: Check one message
muc.text: Find a suspicious message on your phone, ask AI to point out the red flags, then delete it.
